bullets.title: NVDA roadmap confirmed intact; Anthropic compute share rises to ~50%
bullets.body: NVIDIA staff confirmed to multiple accounts that the roadmap is intact and delay reports are false. Separately, Morgan Stanley NDR notes show Anthropic's share of compute running on NVIDIA chips has risen to nearly 50%, described as a notable datapoint on demand concentration. Jensen Huang also characterized as expecting the memory shortage to persist for 'several years.'

bullets.title: NVDA Rubin reportedly delayed again; CPO GPU scale-up also slipping
bullets.body: An expert call flagged another Rubin architecture delay. Separately, a supply chain tracker noted 'CPO GPU scale-up is delayed.' One source added that Micron failed on Rubin specs and NVIDIA subsequently lowered pin speed targets to enable ecosystem shipping. These rumor cycles have become a recurring narrative—'three certainties in life: death, taxes, and NVDA product delay rumors.'

bullets.title: NVDA outperforms AMD on vLLM Kimi benchmark; B300 faster than B200
bullets.body: Alert from a chip-tracking account: on vLLM Kimi (same architecture as xAI's Cursor Compose), NVIDIA 'mogs' AMD with B300 clocking faster than B200, reinforcing NVIDIA's near-term inference leadership over AMD.

bullets.title: META +19% in July; 200-day MA reclaimed at widest margin since January
bullets.body: META reclaimed its 200-day moving average and traded 19% higher month-to-date through the week, the largest gain since April 2025. Unusual million-dollar far-OTM call prints were flagged before the weekend. Separately, SemiAnalysis posted a positive report on META's AI compute buildout—including a plan to double capacity to 14GW by 2027 and begin production of the in-house 'Iris' AI chip in September—cited as a key catalyst.

bullets.title: META: EU risks €12B fine for addictive feeds; halts AI deepfake image tool
bullets.body: EU regulators demanded Meta dismantle addictive design features on Instagram and Facebook, citing potential €12B fine. Separately, Meta reversed a decision allowing AI deepfakes of public accounts on Instagram amid backlash, and halted an AI image tool. Tencent is also reportedly leading a deal to unwind Meta's $2B Manus acquisition.

bullets.title: Micron announces $250B US investment; concrete poured for NY fab
bullets.body: Micron officially poured concrete for its first New York fab in Clay and announced a $250B US manufacturing commitment through 2035. CEO appearance framed as a major milestone. Fintwit notes MU 'will likely make more money in 2026 than the past 35 years combined.' Wells Fargo raised Western Digital (peer) PT to $730 from $575 on the memory cycle.

bullets.title: SK Hynix $26.5B US ADR debut; CEO warns memory crunch past 2030
bullets.body: SK Hynix priced its Nasdaq ADR at $149 (7x oversubscribed), opened at $170 (+14%), and the session closed +13%—the largest US equity offering by a foreign company, topping Alibaba's 2014 IPO. The CEO warned the memory chip shortage may persist past 2030, and characterized 2027 as the worst year from a supply perspective. Analyst community noted the debut boosted investor appetite for the AI trade broadly.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex expected to beat consensus again in 2026/2027
bullets.body: One macro-tech account maintains a long basket of NVDA/MU/SNDK/LITE, predicting US hyperscalers will raise 2026 full-year capex estimates and set 2027 indications above consensus. AI infrastructure demand is broadening beyond frontier labs to neoclouds, European data centers, sovereign compute, and enterprise coding. Separately, Apollo flagged that hyperscaler AI-related capital needs are already extending beyond the USD IG bond market.

bullets.title: AAPL sues OpenAI over hardware trade secret theft; 400 former Apple employees at OpenAI
bullets.body: Apple filed a federal lawsuit against OpenAI alleging misappropriation of trade secrets, naming Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan and engineer Chang Liu (8-year iPhone veteran). Apple also alleges OpenAI asked hiring candidates for confidential hardware/design materials and queried suppliers on restricted metal-finishing methods. OpenAI has reportedly hired 400 people from Apple.

bullets.title: AAPL secures semiconductor tariff exemption in exchange for Intel fab commitments
bullets.body: Per WSJ, Apple secured an exemption from semiconductor tariffs in exchange for committing to manufacture both Mac and iPhone chips at Intel fabs. Apple stock hit record highs on AI momentum tailwinds this week.

bullets.title: MSFT: GPT-5.6 now preferred model in 365 Copilot; UK designates MSFT as critical third party
bullets.body: GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot per OpenAI's Sam Altman. Separately, UK financial regulators designated Microsoft (alongside Google Cloud, Amazon, Oracle) as a critical third party to the UK financial sector, with formal oversight beginning July 13.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $85B equity issuance cited as peak signal; interest expense up 15x YoY
bullets.body: One macro account argues financial asset prices peaked the day Google announced its $85B equity issuance, with supply drag now the primary headwind. Google's quarterly interest expense exceeded $500M, up 15x YoY, driven by AI infrastructure financing. Taiwan has replaced China as the third-largest source of US imports, driven by advanced semiconductor (ATP) imports touching $100B in May.

bullets.title: TSLA: Elon silent on Optimus; robotaxi broken promises resurface; Model S/X line closing
bullets.body: Multiple bear accounts flagged Tesla's reduced Optimus demonstrations and questioned whether silence signals a lack of AI breakthrough. Musk's unfulfilled 2020 promise of 1M robotaxis also recirculated. Tesla is decommissioning the original Model S & X assembly line within 46 days. Australia's Tesla Megapack reached 10 GWh operational capacity. Tesla and SpaceX were asked to evaluate (not mandated to use) Grok 4.5.

bullets.title: TSLA autonomous competition: Google, Amazon, Baidu completing 1M+ unsupervised rides
bullets.body: Bear accounts argued TSLA bulls are deluding themselves about a lack of competition, comparing the situation to 2020-2021 EV scaling debates. Google, Pony, Baidu, and Amazon are reportedly completing over 1 million paid unsupervised autonomous rides, with competitors described as 'easily exceeding TSLA' on that metric.

bullets.title: HOOD: 70K+ Agentic Trading accounts; Robinhood Chain hits $633M DEX volume
bullets.body: Robinhood reports more than 70,000 Agentic Trading accounts opened since May launch, with expansion to crypto for eligible US customers. Robinhood Chain DEX volume hit $633M with 306.5K daily active users. ETH bridged to Robinhood Chain L2 surged ~10x in one week to exceed $100M. CEO Vlad Tenev also promoted Trump Accounts as an ownership vehicle.

bullets.title: MRVL lands 5M tower PIC shipments; Lumentum flags InP capacity expansion
bullets.body: Marvell secured 5 million tower PIC shipments for AI data center optics. Lumentum separately flagged InP (Indium Phosphide) capacity expansion on recent calls, with a VCSEL-based optical interconnect presentation scheduled at LightCounting for July 15. One analyst called InP 'transitioning from optics subtopic to a physical AI infrastructure bottleneck.'

bullets.title: Optical/photonics sector weak; Rosenblatt says short sellers lack conviction
bullets.body: Rosenblatt argued that optical sector weakness from AAOI to LITE is overdone, characterizing CPO delay reports and China capacity fears as drivers but noting short sellers 'do not strongly believe in their thesis' and plan to cover before earnings. One fintwit account observed photonics/optical stocks testing three-month lows, calling it too early to call a bottom.

bullets.title: Semis saw largest weekly net inflows but remain net-sold over past month by hedge funds
bullets.body: Per Goldman Prime data cited in a retweet, Semis & Semi Equipment was the most net bought subsector of the week but remains 'heavily net sold' by hedge funds over the trailing month. Semiconductor stocks have moved ±3% on 15 of the last 30 trading days, a frequency not seen since the dot-com bubble.

bullets.title: Brad Gerstner: companies pay 5x more for best AI; Anthropic ARR hits $69B
bullets.body: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner said companies will pay 5x more for best-in-class AI models and open source has not created pricing pressure, with cheap tokens sufficient only for commodity tasks. Separately, Yipit estimates Anthropic's ARR has reached $69B with daily ARR growth accelerating from ~$400M to ~$550M MoM.

bullets.title: 30-year real yields push to multi-decade highs; Shiller PE nearing dot-com peak
bullets.body: 30-year real yields are pushing back toward multi-decade highs, and the 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.058%—highest since the pre-GFC era. The Shiller PE ratio is 'on the verge of taking out its Dot Com Bubble all-time high.' Q2 tech was the only S&P 500 sector to outperform the index—first such occurrence since at least 1990—while Q2 top performers are broadly lagging in Q3 as rebalancing rotates allocations.
